# Requirements Quality Checklist: Learner Dashboard

**Purpose**: Formal, exhaustive requirements-quality review of the full spec ahead of `/speckit-analyze` -- completeness, clarity, consistency, measurability, scenario/edge-case coverage, non-functional coverage, dependencies, and ambiguities.
**Created**: 2026-08-17
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.
**Resolution pass (2026-08-17)**: At the reviewer's explicit request, every item below was evaluated against spec.md as edited in this session and checked off with a note on where it was resolved. `tasks.md` was also updated (T010, T031) to keep task coverage in sync with the two newly-added testable requirements (US1 Acceptance Scenario 3, FR-010).

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Are subject-section ordering requirements specified for when more than two subjects exist? [Gap, Spec §FR-001] -- Resolved: FR-001 now specifies sections are ordered by `subject_id`.
- [x] CHK002 Is retry/recovery behavior specified for a section in its "couldn't load" failure state (automatic retry, manual retry action, or none until the next full page load)? [Gap, Spec §FR-007, §FR-008] -- Resolved: new FR-010 states no auto-retry; the next full page load is the only retry mechanism.
- [x] CHK003 Are requirements defined for a subject whose content artifact is later invalidated/removed after already being shown to a learner, as distinct from a topic being added/removed within a still-valid subject? [Gap, Spec §Edge Cases] -- Resolved: new Edge Case added.
- [x] CHK004 Are requirements defined for a validated subject whose content artifact has zero topics? [Gap, Spec §FR-001] -- Resolved: new Edge Case added.
- [x] CHK005 Does the Assumptions section list every agent this feature actually depends on, given FR-003/FR-008 both rely on the Sequencing Agent's selection logic but only the Recommendation Agent is named? [Gap, Spec §Assumptions] -- Resolved (during `/speckit-analyze` remediation, prior to this checklist pass): Sequencing Agent added to Assumptions.

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK006 Is "each load" in FR-002/FR-006 precisely scoped (full page navigation vs. component remount vs. tab refocus) so "fresh on each load" is unambiguous? [Clarity, Spec §FR-002, §FR-006] -- Resolved: FR-002 now defines "each load" explicitly.
- [x] CHK007 Is "verbatim" in FR-002 defined precisely enough to distinguish an allowed formatting/rendering change from a disallowed content change? [Clarity, Spec §FR-002] -- Resolved: FR-002 now defines "verbatim" as exact text content, independent of formatting.
- [x] CHK008 Is the required display order of the up-to-3 "upcoming topics" specified -- must the Sequencing Agent's ranking order be visually preserved? [Clarity, Spec §FR-003] -- Resolved: FR-003 now requires ranked order, most-likely-next first.
- [x] CHK009 Is "no indefinite caching" (FR-006) precise enough to rule out or permit short-lived client-side memoization within a single render? [Clarity, Spec §FR-006] -- Resolved: FR-006 now explicitly rules out HTTP caching and any client-side memoization surviving beyond a single page load.

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK010 Do FR-007 and FR-008's failure-state descriptions ("distinct, clear failure state") require consistent presentation across both, or may each section's failure state look and read differently? [Consistency, Spec §FR-007, §FR-008] -- Resolved: new FR-010 requires a shared presentation pattern (also now tracked by tasks.md T031).
- [x] CHK011 Read together, do FR-006's "no caching, fresh on every load" and the Assumptions' "acceptable staleness is as of last page load" describe one unambiguous freshness contract, or could a reader see tension between them? [Consistency, Spec §FR-006, §Assumptions] -- Resolved: the two-tabs Edge Case now explicitly reconciles the two ("stale" = not yet reloaded, never "loaded but wrong").
- [x] CHK012 Is the illustrative/subject-to-change disclosure (FR-004) required to use consistent wording/placement across every subject section, or may each section phrase it independently? [Consistency, Spec §FR-004] -- Resolved: FR-004 now requires the same wording and placement across every section.

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [x] CHK013 Can SC-001's "no drift beyond the current request" be objectively measured without further definition of the current-request boundary? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001] -- Resolved: SC-001 now defines the boundary as the moment of that section's own fetch, with later writes reflected only on the next load.
- [x] CHK014 Is SC-002's "without error" defined precisely enough to be objectively pass/fail (zero unhandled exceptions vs. zero non-2xx responses across all per-subject calls)? [Measurability, Spec §SC-002] -- Resolved: SC-002 now defines "without error" precisely and excludes FR-007/FR-008's deliberate failure states by definition.
- [x] CHK015 Is SC-005's "renders... correctly" independently measurable, or does it rely entirely on FR-001/FR-002/FR-003 being separately verified elsewhere? [Measurability, Spec §SC-005] -- Resolved: SC-005 now explicitly cross-references FR-001/FR-002/FR-003 as what "correctly" means.

## Scenario Coverage

- [x] CHK016 Is a scenario defined for a learner with data in one subject but zero data in another, so a populated section and a "just getting started" section render side by side in the same load? [Coverage, Gap, Spec §US1, §US4] -- Resolved: new US1 Acceptance Scenario 3 added (and now tracked by tasks.md T010).
- [x] CHK017 Are the interaction effects defined for when the brand-new-learner state (FR-005) and a section failure state (FR-007/FR-008) occur simultaneously? [Coverage, Gap] -- Resolved: new Edge Case + FR-007 amendment establish failure-state precedence over FR-005's empty-state framing.
- [x] CHK018 Is a scenario defined for a learner answering a question in one subject while another subject's section is still loading on the same dashboard page? [Coverage, Gap] -- Resolved: new Edge Case clarifies this isn't reachable within this milestone's UI (answering happens on a separate `/practice` page).

## Edge Case Coverage

- [x] CHK019 Is the "two browser tabs" edge case's staleness allowance reconciled with FR-006's "no caching, fresh on every load" -- i.e., does staleness apply only across loads, never within one? [Edge Case, Consistency, Spec §Edge Cases, §FR-006] -- Resolved: same fix as CHK011.
- [x] CHK020 Is a race condition addressed where a learner submits an answer while the dashboard's mastery-state fetch for that same subject is already in flight? [Edge Case, Gap] -- Resolved: same fix as CHK018 -- not reachable by construction.
- [x] CHK021 Is the case of a platform with only one validated subject addressed -- does the multi-subject combined view degrade sensibly to a single section? [Edge Case, Gap] -- Resolved: new Edge Case added.

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [x] CHK022 Is a performance/latency expectation stated for the dashboard's per-subject, multi-call load, or is the absence of one an explicit stated assumption rather than silence? [Gap, Non-Functional] -- Resolved: new Assumption states this explicitly as a scope decision.
- [x] CHK023 Are accessibility requirements (keyboard navigation across sections, screen-reader behavior for a failure state) specified anywhere in this spec? [Gap, Non-Functional] -- Resolved: new Assumption explicitly defers accessibility requirements for this milestone.
- [x] CHK024 Are requirements defined for how many subject sections the dashboard must support before a different presentation (pagination, collapsing) is needed? [Gap, Non-Functional, Scalability] -- Resolved: new Assumption states the small-subject-count scope decision.

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [x] CHK025 Is the assumption that "every subject with a content artifact" is a small, bounded set (currently two) stated anywhere as an explicit scale assumption? [Assumption, Gap] -- Resolved: same fix as CHK024.
- [x] CHK026 Is the dependency on each subject's prerequisite graph being acyclic/fully reachable (required for FR-003's upcoming-topics selection to terminate) stated as an assumption, or only implied by inheriting Milestone 1's content-artifact validation? [Assumption, Spec §FR-003] -- Resolved: new Assumption states this explicitly, citing spec 001 FR-002.
- [x] CHK027 Is it explicit that this feature introduces no new persisted entity and depends only on read access to Milestone 1's and the Recommendation Agent's existing data, with no migration assumed? [Assumption, Spec §Key Entities] -- Resolved: new Assumption states this explicitly, alongside the existing Key Entities language.

## Ambiguities & Conflicts

- [x] CHK028 Is "the platform" in FR-001/FR-009 ("subjects... in the platform") defined precisely, distinguishing it from "subjects the learner is engaged with"? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-001] -- Resolved: FR-001 now defines "the platform" explicitly.
- [x] CHK029 Is a requirement/acceptance-criteria ID scheme established that lets each User Story's acceptance scenarios trace to the specific FR(s) and SC(s) they validate? [Traceability, Gap] -- Resolved: every Acceptance Scenario across all four User Stories now cites its own spec's FR number(s).
- [x] CHK030 Is it clear whether "just getting started" (FR-005) and the Recommendation Agent's "insufficient data" framing (reused verbatim per FR-002) are the same concept displayed once, or two distinct pieces of text a learner could see worded differently in the same section? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-002, §FR-005] -- Resolved: FR-005 now clarifies the Recommendation Agent's framing IS the on-page text, not a second layered message.

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify` (not present for this feature; unrelated to this file)
- Two resolutions (CHK016, CHK010) added new testable spec content (US1 Acceptance Scenario 3; FR-010) that in turn required updating `tasks.md` (T010 extended, T031 added) to keep task coverage in sync -- a reminder that resolving a requirements-quality gap can itself introduce new coverage obligations downstream
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
